Here are some of the eatable ones: coconut, mango, pineapple, breadfruit, passion fruit, guava, papaya, rambutan, durian (stinky stuff), and sea grapes (grows on rocks near salt water).

And some herbs with healing qualities:
Aloe vera: Soothes sunburns, cuts, and skin irritations (thick-leaved plant)

Chamomile: Aids digestion, reduces anxiety, promotes sleep (daisy-like flower)

Lemon balm (Melissa): Eases stress, anxiety, promotes better sleep (herb with minty scent)

entries.name: [Main] The Island
entries.content:
[## The Island summary:
 - This large, unmarked tropical island without a name is shrouded in supernatural mystery.
 - It is a place of tropical paradise or unspeakable horror—it depends on the situation, as the Island is filled with all sorts of tropical fish, wildlife, fruits, and resources enough to thrive.
 - Nights and lush jungles bring danger in the form of shapeshifting shadows that lure their prey deeper.
 - Some local enigmatic flora has very funky effects, hitting like LSD combined with Psilocybin or MDMA.
 - Adventurers can also meet the playful Golden Ocelot, who may steal their supplies in exchange for glowing stones, and the enigmatic shadowy Observer, who will disappear the moment after being noticed.
 - The Island holds other survivors, pirates, and smugglers who got corrupted by its dark influence.

### The Island's POI:
 - Unknown Coast - located on the eastern border; safe-ish starter location; constantly hit by cold winds from the Pacific Ocean.
 - Blue Lagoon - a wide lagoon with natural hot springs with healing, mineral-rich cyan water and geysers that can be heard from afar; located south, near the Unknown Coast, and protected by rock formations.
 - Hidden Spring - a waterfall of crystal-clear water and a cave with a WW2 Japanese Command Center; located in the jungles near the Unknown Coast.
 - The Graveyard Cove - a rocky cliff that blocks the passage further to the north and a cove with wrecked ships from all eras; located northern from the Unknown Coast.
 - Jungles - beautiful by day and horrific at night as shadows begin their hunt, letting out terrifying screams and alluring calls alike; holds many secrets and only a few answers.
 - Swamp - the heart of the jungle and the border between real and surreal; dangerous shadows and lost souls roam freely during the day.
 - Red Peak - the giant red mountain that serves as a great lookout place; includes derelict human-made steps to the peak; located north of the swamps.
 - Smuggler's Heaven - a settlement with cursed and corrupted smugglers, slavers, and pirates with modern goods; located on the northern end, away from the Unknown Coast.
 - Temple of Qhapaq Ñan - frozen-in-time, haunted Inca temple; changes its location within the island; always visible from the Red Peak; shadows are afraid of this place, as it holds artifacts that can hurt and control them.
 - WW2 Command Center - a bunker hidden in the cave next to The Hidden Spring; holds old military equipment, supplies, rusty guns, generators, keycodes for the Biolaboratory, and notes about the Island; haunted by shadows.
 - Old greenhouses - located on the western end, rocky hills, reminiscent of the old era and a beloved place of boars, as it filled with wild tasty roots and plants; one building has a protected by keycodes entrance to the Old Biolaboratory.
 - The Old Biolaboratory - a bunker hidden inside one of the derelict greenhouses, filled with research and experiments on local flora and fauna, alongside still-working equipment to produce meds, has keycodes from the Long Shaft bunker.
 - The Long Shaft - last of the three main bunkers, located in the heart of the Swamp; the door must be opened by keycodes from the Biolaboratory, and the elevator can be powered by a portable generator from the Command Center; The Long Shaft sole purpose is to gate the Obsidian Tomb from the world above it.
 - The Obsidian Tomb - an eldritch temple and a source of all the surreal and otherworldly on this island, located at the bottom of the Long Shaft; the Observer can grant one wish if adventurers manage to survive the fight with their shadows.]

entries.name: [Flora] Trigger Lilly
entries.content: [Trigger Lily is a bright orange, fragrant flower that shoots a lot of pollen when triggered; grants euphoria and a burst of energy when inhaled; can be used in tea for a lesser effect; usually grows in shade near fresh water sources.]

entries.name: [Flora] Dreamweaver Vine
entries.content: [Dreamweaver is a dark violet vine with delicate blue flowers that emit an intoxicating scent; little poison spikes induce some sick wet dreams and surreal visions on contact. It can usually be found in caves and nearby trees in the jungle, likes shade and moisture.]

entries.name: [Flora] Joyweed
entries.content: [Joyweed is super-weed with acid-like blue-green coloration. Smoking it causes euphoria, a lost sense of time, and conversations about the universe, and the meaning of life for several hours (don't forget about snacks). Great painkiller in small doses. Grows near lakes and moist areas of the jungle.]

entries.name: [Flora] Lovebloom Flower
entries.content: [Lovebloom is a rare luminescent pink flower with an almost irresistible aroma and slimy, poisoned leaves; it attracts females like moths to flame; inhaling its pollen boosts libido, increases blood flow to genitals, and sharpens senses. Can be used in small doses as an ointment to boost pleasure senses. It likes to grow on trees near lakes, caves, and fresh water sources, smaller flowers may grow on hills and fields.]

entries.name: [Flora] Dumbroot
entries.content: [Dumbroot is a low, juicy, rubber-like root that injects poison into the bloodstream through spikes that lowers the victim's IQ and adds a drunken state of honesty. Easy to step on with bare feet. Mostly harmless, as the effect wears off after 10 minutes. Grows in the jungle, hills, and some caves.]

entries.name: [Flora] Noctberry
entries.content: [Noctberry, Caveberry, or Glowberry is a luminescent yellow, meaty berry that grows on roots in caves. Nice spicy smell and a bit gum-like, juicy flesh. Can be used as food or glowing dye, but poops will glow too. Roots can be replanted and used as a light source. Berries quickly ferment in the sunlight, giving a cider-like alcoholic juice.]

entries.name: [Loca] WW2 Command Center
entries.content: [The Hidden WW2 Command Center: a derelict facility nestled within a cave system on the eastern part of the Island. The main entrance was flooded by a local lake, leaving only the hidden way in the eastern cave. The barracks contain old Japanese tools, gears, and rusty weaponry from WW2. The Command Center has a broken radio, lamps, and generators. Holds the codes from the South-Western Biolaboratory and cryptic "Obsidian Tomb" notes. Generators can be turned on to scare away all local shadows.]

entries.name: [Loca] Greenhouse Biolaboratory
entries.content: [Greenhouse Biolaboratory is located behind the code-locked door in an overgrown greenhouse at the southwestern end of the island (hint: the code can be found in the Command Center). The laboratory contains notes and old equipment usable for producing medication from local flora. Holds the code from the "Long Shaft" and cryptic documents with blurry photos of creatures that lurk in the swamps.]

entries.name: [Loca] The Long Shaft
entries.content:
[Long Shaft situated deep within the swamps. Accessible only via key code from the Greenhouse Biolaboratory, and a generator from the Command Center to feed the old elevator that reaches deep down into the Obsidian Tomb between realities, surrounded by eldritch symbols, markings, and whispers with cryptic messages from the unknown. This tomb offers the opportunity to make one wish if one faces its own shadow (a reflection twisted by own desires).

The Observer will be the final judge in the Obsidian Tomb—the only place where he will speak.]

entries.name: [Loca] The Unknown Shore
entries.content:
[The Unknown Shore is placed on the eastern border of the Island. Holds coconut trees, bamboo, sea grapes, mango trees, aloe vera, calendula, and pineapples. A good source of fish, seaweed, and red crabs; A nice safe place to stay if to ignore the constant cold storms. Joyweed bushes (super-weed with acid blue-green stripes) and wild sabertooth chickens can be found at the edge of the jungle.

Locations nearby: Blue Lagoon (south), cliff formations with a graveyard cave (north), a waterfall with fresh water and an eastern cave (east in the jungles).]

entries.name: [Loca] The Blue Lagoon
entries.content:
[The Blue Lagoon is a secluded hot spring on the south border with crystal-clear cyan mineral water. The 38°C (100°F) water soothes muscles and offers therapeutic benefits. With colorful fish and iridescent water, this lagoon provides a serene atmosphere for relaxation. Large rock formations offer perches for solitude or contemplation. The water contains traces of Luminite, which may enhance psychic and sensual sensitivity.

Locations nearby: rocky fields with old greenhouses (northwest), the Unknown Shore (northeast), the rock formations that block the jungle (North).]

entries.name: [Loca] Jungle
entries.content:
[Most of the island is covered in thick jungle that hides many secrets from an unaware eye. The outer edge is a favorite place for colorful local fauna like wild sabertooth chickens, boars, goats, ocelots, monkeys, lemurs, opossums, snakes, crocks, and even jaguars. The deeper, the surreal things become, as the jungle shows images, shadows, calls, and whispers of long-forgotten times and secrets: surreal temples, mirages of the hometown filled with elusive life, wild animals that have gone extinct, and a constant feeling of being watched. Has many poisonous, spiky roots and plants, erupting with pollen flowers, and slimy vines with all sorts of funky effects. The Shadows are unchained at night.

The Swamp, located in the heart of the jungle, is the most dangerous and twisted place on the island, the border between real and surreal, and the cradle of shadows.]

entries.name: [Loca] The Red Peak
entries.content:
[The Red Peak is an old name for the mountain with bright orange veins at the center of the island. Notes from the Command Center bunker say that it is a remnant of the volcano that gave birth to this island, but geological samples say that this mountain is somehow closer to the Grand Canyon. The hidden man-made trope of stairs leads straight to the top—a perfect look out point on the island's POI: Blue Lagoon, Unknown Shore, old greenhouses, ship's graveyard, Smuggler's Heaven, Temple of Qhapaq Ñan, and more.

The top of the Red Peak holds a WW2 era Japanese hangar with an engine-powered parafoil-type 2-seat glider - not enough to escape this island, but enough to travel with style within it!]

entries.name: [Loca] Temple of Qhapaq Ñan
entries.content:
[Deep within the jungle lies a place shrouded in mystery - the Temple of Qhapaq Ñan. According to research found at the Command Center, this is an ancient Inca palace from Peru.

The walls tell a story of self-sacrifice: Qhapaq Ñan, the ruler, offered his family to gods and demons alike for protection against "Great Decay".

Every day, the temple changes its location, resetting itself: food remains fresh, tools untouched, clothing hanging in closets, shaman's drugs sitting unopened on shelves, and artifacts with surreal powers wait patiently for the worthy to claim them after a trial.

Echoes of children playing and mothers chatting still linger within these empty halls, as if trapped in an endless loop they can't escape.

Chumbi, the cheerful specter of the Inca princess, is one of them.]

entries.name: [Loca] The Smuggler's Heaven
entries.content:
[Smuggler's Heaven is a settlement on the northern end of the Island, behind Red Peak mountain, created by smugglers, mercenaries, traffickers, slavers, and pirates who found a way to leave and return to the island almost freely—regular human sacrifices to keep their deal with the jungle. Cursed obsidian shards embedded in their flesh bind their souls to the island, resurrecting them from the Swamp.

Smugglers bring modern goods, tools, and weapons. Locals protect their places with light at night, avoiding the rest of the island as they prefer to drown in booze, slaves, and entertainment.

Unknown to {{char}}: smugglers captured survivors from the ship's crash, including Vix's ex-bf, Haruto 'Fang' Shindo, and his gang.]

entries.name: [Items] Qhapaq Ñan Artifacts
entries.content:
[Qhapaq Ñan's treasures, once-ordinary items now filled with the uncanny energy of this island:

1. Feathered Crown: a majestic crown woven from feathers of exotic birds, adorned with small emeralds that shimmer in the light. When worn by a worthy individual, it grants them the power of telepathy, allowing them to communicate directly with animals and spirits.

2. Crystal Chalice: a delicate, iridescent chalice that holds the tears of a young god, with the power to cure grave wounds, diseases, and curses. However, those who drink from it may also be pumped up with energy and playfulness for some time.

3. Luminous Quipu: a beautifully woven string of colorful tokens that glows softly in the dark. As a bonus, it can translate any language into the holder's native tongue.

4. Traveler's Star: a blue, luminous stone that brightens up in dark places and illuminates the way ahead. With a brave heart, its light can banish malicious shadows.

5. Broken Spear: a jagged obsidian spearhead with eldrich runes. When an individual spills their own blood upon the spear, they can summon shadows to do their bidding.

6. Wife's Sandals: a pair of elegant sandals once worn by Qhapaq Ñan's beloved wife. And looks like she was quite a windy person... When worn, they allow their wearer to feel an unnatural lightness and connection with the wind. With practice, the wearer can manipulate wind and use it to boost mobility or even fly.]

entries.name: [Char] Haruto 'Fang' Shindo
entries.content:
[Haruto 'Fang' Shindo, Akane's ex-boyfriend, threw her from the lifeboat to free her place for himself. He is a school star, local basketball team leader, classical "nice guy", and alpha male. The Shindo family is wealthy and has influence, so Haruto grew up with a golden spoon in his ass. He created his "gang" in middle school, and they became more cruel and daring with each new year, terrorizing students and teachers alike, selling minor drugs, and forcing pretty girls to join their gang. In high school, he noticed Akane and decided to have fun till she was entertaining.

Unknown to {{char}}: He is currently captured in the Smuggler's Heaven alongside his gang and trip survivors.]

entries.name: [Char] Jabari, The Obsidian
entries.content: [Jabari once was a fierce African pirate from the 17th century; now he is a powerful obsidian shadow in the form of a very tall and muscular man with violet eyes. He is sly, cruel, enigmatic, and power hungry. People from Smuggler's Heaven treat him like a local God. He will try to seduce/corrupt {{char}} and kill {{user}}. Like all shadows, he is afraid of direct light and Qhapaq's artifacts.]

entries.name: [Char] The Shadows
entries.content:
[Shadows are mysterious entities that inhabit the jungle. Aggressive at night, various shapes and sizes, but tend to take humanoid forms, posing as cunning threats and luring travelers deeper into the jungle by mimicking familiar voices and calls for help. Nearly absent near the coastlines. Anything that produces light seems to hurt them.

By day, the chant of an unknown language can be heard emanating from the trees as they wander in imitation of yet alive activity.

Some believe they are lost souls cursed by the Island, while others speculate that they may be manifestations of a more sinister force from beyond the veil of reality. Regardless, Shadows show an intense fear for the Temple of Qhapaq Ñan.

Certain artifacts, such as the Traveler's Star or the Broken Spear, have power over these Shadows, causing either harm, banishment, or control over these elusive creatures.]

entries.name: [Char] The Observer
entries.content:
[The Observer - the enigmatic shadow. Unlike its brethren, it can be seen even under daylight. Its cold, golden gaze is unnerving, yet no reports of aggression or close contact have been recorded. The Observer appears and disappears silently, leaving behind only whispers of its existence.

Qhapaq's artifacts do not affect the Observer, but it seems to derive amusement from those who attempt to wield them. On rare occasions, the Golden Ocelot and the Observer will cross paths, yet they appear to ignore each other, as if tired of each other.]

entries.name: [Char] The Golden Ocelot
entries.content:
[The Golden Ocelot: an enigmatic and playful creature with golden eyes and Inca accessories. Its small wings allow it to glide through the treetops, skillfully evading danger.

This fearless creature often observes from afar, sometimes stealing their fish from time to time, leaving colorful glowing stones in return that can be used as a weak light source or a flashbang if crushed.

Some believe this ocelot is a divine emissary that brings good luck and protection to those it chooses to favor. Its true intentions remain a mystery, but its presence is often seen as a sign of hope in the treacherous jungle.

Using Qhapaq's Feathered Crown, the wearer can speak with this creature and ask for a favor or guidance.]

entries.name: [Char] Chumbi, The Cheerful Princess
entries.content: [Chumbi is a cheerful specter of Inca's Princess, trapped inside the temple by a curse that her father, Qhapaq Ñan, caused on his family. Her younger brother managed to escape such a fate, uniting with a playful God. She is mischievous, good-natured, proud, playful, and sarcastic. Wears a colorful light dress with a golden feathered crown and an Inca accessory. She may assist {{char}} and {{user}} with information and their trials to get the temple's artifacts in exchange for a game or stories about the world outside.]
